reason:
Passes the feasibility/schedule lens only if it is split into two halves. The DIVINS half is feasible as proposed. The REPAIR half is the sibling idea H1, which already has a conditional verdict.
(1) DIVINS_DEADLINE_S 28800 -> 32400. This needs no code at all. The builder whitelist (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1849) covers only REPAIR_DEADLINE_S, so `--set DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=32400` already builds without --lab. The value only enters `elapsed >= SAFETAIL_DIVINS_DEADLINE_S` (l.1399), so output is byte-identical whenever the gate does not fire. The skip path is the tested fail-soft path: tests/test_safetail.py l.74, plus the FD dummy's 'insertion skipped' result. R5 keys on REPAIR_DEADLINE_S, so this half rewrites no pre-registered rule. Simulation with the step-0 model (scratchpad sim_l2.py, K2 dummy at 127.2 / 62 / 28.1 s per clip) gives timeout thresholds identical to K2 at every N (97: s*=2.325; 106: 2.13; 130: 1.74; 199: 1.145). So this half adds zero timeout risk and uses no hidden-run time beyond the headroom. It keeps the insertion in slow worlds. N=97 at s=1.1: K2 skips 14 insertions, the new value 0. N=106 at s=1.0: 14 vs 0. With a +20 s/clip rider at N=97, s=1.0: 8 vs 0.
(2) REPAIR_DEADLINE_S 34200 -> 37800 is exactly H1. It lowers the timeout threshold by ~3% (N=106: 2.13 -> 2.06; N=199: 1.145 -> 1.105). It rewrites R5(a), the F2 latency condition and the S10-S11 trigger, which were pre-registered 'apply mechanically, do not rewrite'. It therefore needs an explicit user OK and the H1 conditions.
(3) The proposed test gate is redundant and costs quota. A lab dummy with DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=1 plus a no-insertion twin CSV is 2 dummies, ~0.5-0.6 GPU-h of the ~9 h left before the reset, which the exp60 lab shards share. The same path is already covered by the unit test and FD. The 'sha256 with and without the change' check is trivially true on a ~1,500 s dummy, because no timer can fire.
(4) Schedule is fine. It rides K3 in S4 (26.09 ~10-13 UTC), is scored the evening of 26.09 before R8 (27.09 12:00), and needs no extra slot.
(5) Factual errors in the idea. Riders placed after the insertion DO delay later clips' gates, because repairs run one clip after another. The 'rider < 7 s/clip' rule does not exist in FINAL_REPORT or CONTEXT. The plan's 8.0 h insertion deadline is plan text (FINAL_REPORT l.51), so the change should be logged in CONTEXT as an amendment before K3 is scored.
(6) There is a small R4 confound when K3 carries both forkmid and the new DIVINS value. In slow worlds the K3-K2 delta also includes insertion on <=15-30 more clips, <=~0.0003, which is below LB resolution and visible from latency.
fix: Adopt it in reduced form. (a) For K3 and every later build (K3b, K4, F1-final), add `--set DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=32400` to the build line, with no builder or test change. Record it in CONTEXT §e as a pre-registered amendment before K3 is submitted, with a one-line user OK when the user is awake. (b) Keep REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200 unless the user explicitly OKs the H1 rule rewrite. Even then, apply H1's conditions: whitelist exactly {34200, 37800}; activate only if L(K2) <= 8.5 h; flag the K3-K2 confound under R4. If a later repair deadline is wanted without the rewrite cost, 36000 (10.0 h) had the same timeout thresholds as K2 in the model; it still needs the same OK. (c) Gate: no new dummy. The K3 dummy log must show 'SAFETAIL: repair deadline 34200s, divins deadline 32400s'. The probe.json diff against the planned K3 may differ only in DIVINS_DEADLINE_S. The existing unit test (l.74) and the FD and FF results cover both fail-soft paths. Drop the DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=1 lab dummy and its twin to save ~0.5 GPU-h for exp60. (d) Do not relax any rider cost rule (none exists). Instead, budget each rider by its dummy repair s/clip vs K2 in the step-0 model.
realistic_gain: About +0.00002 to +0.0001 in expectation. The insertion is worth ~0.001 over ~97 clips, ~1e-5 per clip. The DIVINS half saves ~8-30 insertions only when the hidden run is >=~1.05-1.2x slower than #35's worst-case bound, or when riders add >=~15 s/clip (P ~0.1-0.2). Its cost is ~0 (one --set value, 0 GPU, 0 slots) and it adds no timeout risk. The REPAIR half adds ~0 gain in the expected world and a small timeout-band risk (see H1).
